items.title: Kristen Korb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000
items.q: I heard the choir sing “Save the Bones for Henry Jones/’Cause Henry Don’t Eat No Meat,” and I don’t know why but it just knocked me out.

ctx.x: Well that’s why we’re here. Tell me where you were born and when.

Well I was born and raised in Montana, the jazz mecca of the west. And actually my family had moved to Boise, Idaho where my father had a western wear store. And that was like through my kindergarten and junior high years. And when I was in sixth grade the junior high choir and band programs came through the schools and I was sitting on the gym floor with all the other kids and I heard the choir sing “Save the Bones for Henry Jones/’Cause Henry Don’t Eat No Meat,” and I don’t know why but it just knocked me out.…

So just the fact that you were up there, and everybody is just smiling at you and being so supportive. And by the time I got done with the song it was like wheew, wow, this is cooool. So I went to camp again the next year, and when I got in the ninth grade our family moved back to Montana. And I thought my jazz career was over because I mean I went back to the sticks again.
